newsitem.title: FINLAND: Novartis deal to help Tamro sales.
newsitem.headline: Novartis deal to help Tamro sales.

text.p: Finnish pharmaceuticals wholesaler Tamro Oy said on Wednesday its expanded distribution deal with Swiss drugs giant Novartis AG would boost sales and have a "positive" impact on earnings.

"It will increase our turnover in Sweden by over 400 million Swedish crowns per year," Tamro's pharma distribution division president Heikki Ojanpera told Reuters by telephone, adding that the estimate was based on 1996 sales.

That would be an uptick of about three percent over its 1996 Swedish pharma distribution sales of 12.7 billion Swedish crowns -- 70 percent of the pharma division's total net sales of 12.34 billion Finnish markka.
The impact on earnings this year would be "positive," Ojanpera said, but declined to elaborate.
He was commenting on news that Tamro expanded a distribution agreement with Novartis to encompass all Novartis drugs sold in Sweden.

Before the deal, Tamro was distributor in Sweden of drugs inherited by Novartis from Ciba Geigy Ag, but did not distribute drugs made by Sandoz AG, Ojanpera said: Ciba and Sandoz merged last year to create Novartis.

"We are now developing Novartis business in this region, starting with... Finland, Sweden and then expanding to Norway as well and gradually step by step to the Baltic states," he said. "It is a process that has just now started."
The Novartis deal was an important step on the way, he said.
Sandoz drugs were previously sold in Sweden by Tamro's competitor KD, Ojanpera said. Now Tamro's wholly-owned subsidiary ADA AB will be the only channel.
Tamro is already sole distributor of Novartis drugs in Finland, but Sweden is Tamro's main market: Finnish sales made up 27 percent of the pharma distribution unit's 1996 sales.

Tamro said on Wednesday its group January-April net sales fell one percent year-on-year and its Swedish pharma sales fell 11 percent mainly because of hoarding of drugs in Sweden at the end of 1996, which hit sales in the first tertial of this year.

Ojanpera said it was too early to say how the Novartis deal would affect total sales this year, or how far it could offset the early-year dip: he noted the whole Swedish market had been depressed in the early part of the year.
